new_statements.quote: Stress. In most languages stress, a slight raise of the pitch, is not relevant. Only PWG has a system that is meaningful even for grammar. The following presentation refers to Inor, where these phenomena were investigated in detail.
new_statements.citation: Hetzron, Robert. 1997. Outer South Ethiopic. In Robert Hetzron (ed.), The Semitic Languages (Routledge Language Family Descriptions), 535-549. London: Routledge.
new_statements.locator: p. 539, section 'Stress' (chapter 23; Masqan listed among the OSE/Western Gurage languages on p. 535)
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Quote check: the excerpt file and the underlying archive.org scanned (ch. 23 'Outer South Ethiopic', printed p. 539, section 'Stress') contain exactly: 'In most languages stress, a slight raise of the pitch, is not relevant. Only PWG has a system that is meaningful even for grammar. The following presentation refers to Inor, where these phenomena were investigated in detail.' -- verbatim as reported. I read the whole ch. 23 phonology section (pp. 535-539): Masqan is listed on p. 535 as the non-CPWG member of Western Gurage; it is named for gemination (p. 537), verb-class alternations and internal labialization (p. 538), but nowhere for stress; the stress rules after the quoted sentence (fin…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Group-level only: across Outer South Ethiopic (Gafat, Soddo, Goggot, Muher, Masqan, Ezha, Chaha etc.) stress is a weak pitch rise without distinctive function; only Peripheral Western Gurage (Inor, Endegen, Gyeto, Ener) has grammatically relevant stress. No stress position is stated for Masqan; the Inor rule (final closed syllable stressed, else penult) is explicitly PWG-specific and must not be transferred to Mesqan.
new_statements.exceptions: PWG (Inor etc.) is the exception with functional stress; hedged 'in most languages'. Consistent with Hetzron 1977 B.1.3 ('hardly been investigated... do not seem to be distinctive. This may be true for most languages of this group') and Leslau 1992[1979] ('Phonemic stress was recorded in Ennemor, Endegeň and Gyeto' only).
new_statements.domain_note: Statement is about the language group, not Mesqan by name; describes stress phonetically as slight pitch raise; word vs phrase domain not specified. All Mesqan-specific descriptions opened (Getachew 2011, Meseret 2012, Ninomiya 2011, Ikeda 2013-2017, Hara 2019/2023, Ousman 2018/2019) are silent; Ninomiya 2011:157 explicitly declines to describe pitch or stress accent.
new_statements.identity_note: All Mesqan-specific sources opened describe the Mesqan/Mäsqan of Butajira town and Mesqan (Meskan) woreda, Gurage Zone = mesq1240. The only stress statement found (Hetzron 1997:539, echoed by Hetzron 1977 B.1.3 and Leslau 1992[1979]) is a group-level remark about Outer South Ethiopic / Gunnän-Gurage as a whole, not about Mesqan by name; the explicit stress rules in the same passage are for Inor (inor1238, Peripheral Western Gurage) and do not apply to Mesqan.
